correctness.rationale: The three partial derivatives of X²Y+XZ²+2Y²Z have no common geometric projective zero: X=0 forces Y=Z=0; after X=1 the first gives Y=3Z², the second Z³=4, and the third Z³=3, impossible over characteristic seven. The twelve-point exhaustive P²(F7) count yields the displayed twelve gradient lines, all distinct. Their product XYZ(X³-Y³)(X³-Z³)(Y³-Z³) vanishes at every rational point since each nonzero cube equals 1 or -1. A smooth conic has 8 tangent lines with no triple concurrence, covering exactly 36<57 points; singular conic tangents cover at most two component lines. The finite incidence and rational-point table are exhaustively replayed by included verify.py.

originality.rationale: The 2023 foundational tangent-filling paper explicitly asks for minimum degree and excludes its own particular degree-six example in characteristic seven, not all degree-three curves. Its degree q-1 construction assumes q >= 11. The independent blocking-set paper distinguishes a cubic point set from the distinct problem of its rational tangent lines. Exact F7 cubic witness, complete tangent list, and sharp lower bound do not follow from these theorems. Research-index similarity searches of the exact finite-field parameter, aliases and dual Fermat realization gave no matching result; unindexed work remains possible.
residual_risks: An older unindexed elliptic cubic with the same twelve tangent lines, a Hesse/Ceva construction, or stronger general theorem may subsume the witness.
No claim of uniqueness or classification of tangent-filling cubics over F7 is made.

value.rationale: Question 1.5 of the 2023 tangent-filling paper asks for the exact minimum degree. The theorem determines that natural extremal invariant at the otherwise uncovered nonsquare field F7, using a three-monomial genus-one witness whose twelve tangents realize a complete Fermat/triangle blocking configuration. This is a sharp algebraic-geometric existence and obstruction result, not an arbitrary invariant of an unmotivated curve or a numerical table recomputation.
